To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of anticonvulsants, such as phenytoin, phenobarbital, and primidone, is associated with a decrease in serum vitamin B12, and this effect is enhanced by folic acid therapy.
the serum folate levels in patients with epilepsy who take anticonvulsants fall when folic acid is added to their treatment.

folic acid supplementation in epileptic patients treated by anticonvulsants is associated with a fall in vitamin B 12 levels, which is not reversed by stopping the folic acid but is reversed by stopping the anticonvulsanthttps://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1569413/.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of anticonvulsants on folate metabolism in epileptic patients.
the effects of folic acid therapy in epileptic patients treated concurrently with anticonvulsive drugs.
the inter‐relations of folic acid and vitamin B12 in epileptic patients receiving anticonvulsants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of phenytoin, phenobarbitone, primidone and carbamazepine, in doses which are effective in the treatment of epilepsy, may cause a fall of vitamin B12 in the serum, and that folic acid therapy, in a dosage of 10–15 mg per day, may cause a similar fall.
folic acid therapy of epileptics treated with anticonvolvants leads to a rapid fall in serum vitamin B12 and a slow fall in serum folate levels.
folic acid and vitamin B12 levels are interrelated, and the administration of one of the vitamins will affect the other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anticonvulsants used in our study are capable of inducing folic acid deficiency in the absence of dietary folate deficiency.
folic acid deficiency may develop in epileptics treated with anticonvolusants, even when their diet is normal, because the drugs interfere with intestinal absorption of folic acid.
folic acid deficiency in patients receiving anticonvulsants may be due to a decrease in vitamin B12 levels, which may be due to the anticonvulsans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamin B12 and folic acid are essential for a healthy brain and body.
the vitamin B12-folate relationship is a complicated one.

the vitamin B12 deficiency in the patients with epilepsy is not only related with the anticonvulsants but also with folate deficiency, and the deficiency of both vitamin B12 and folate may have an important role in the pathogenesis of the epilepsy, and the vitamin B12 supplementation should be given to these patients with epilepsy.
